facts.fact_text: The applicants attended unauthorised opposition demonstrations organised by the Ictimai Palata group, held in Baku on 14 May 2012.
The applicants attended unauthorised opposition demonstrations organised by the Ictimai Palata group, held in Baku on 21 May 2012.
The applicants submitted that the demonstrations had been intended to be peaceful.
The applicants submitted that the demonstrations had been conducted in a peaceful manner.
Shortly after the applicants joined the demonstrations, the police started to disperse the protesters.

According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), shortly after the police operation to disperse the demonstration of 14 May 2012 had started, around six or seven police officers pushed her so that she almost fell off a ladder.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), a police officer, whom she did not know, slapped her neck during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), she was forcibly put on a bus by the police, together with six or seven other female participants in the demonstration of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), during the 21 May 2012 demonstration several police officers swore at her.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), during the 21 May 2012 demonstration several police officers applied physical force to her, as a result of which she had bruises for several months.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), police officers dragged her by both hands to a car during the 21 May 2012 demonstration.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012 a police officer hit her in the knee hard.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012 a police officer swore at her.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), the police forcibly put her on a bus which was being used to remove people from the demonstration venue of 14 May 2012.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), she was taken by the police to the Sabail District Police Office following the 21 May 2012 demonstration.
According to the fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova), during the 21 May 2012 demonstration she was taken to the Sabail District Police Office in order to stop her participation in the demonstration.

The relevant domestic law concerning freedom of assembly and the organisation and holding of public assemblies is summarised in Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, §§ 27-30, 15 October 2015).

According to the Sabail District Court's decision of 23 October 2012, the applicants participated in unauthorised assemblies on 14 and 21 May 2012 and were removed from the venue of the unlawful assembly, by being put on buses, for having violated public order and not obeying the police officers.

According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), shortly after the police operation to disperse the demonstration of 14 May 2012 had started, around six or seven police officers pushed her so that she almost fell off a ladder.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), a police officer, whom she did not know, slapped her neck during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), during the 21 May 2012 demonstration several police officers applied physical force to her, as a result of which she had bruises for several months.

According to the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), police officers intentionally touched some parts of her body to humiliate her as a woman during the 14 May 2012 demonstration, including pressing her breasts.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012 a police officer hit her in the knee hard.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012 a police officer swore at her.
According to the fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova), when she tried to escape from a police officer during the 14 May 2012 demonstration, the police officer stepped on her foot to stop her.
The Sabail District Court held on 23 October 2012 that the applicants' claims of having been subjected to attacks and ill-treatment by the police officers concerned had not been proved.
